claims.content: To diagnose a failed device by identifying the specific failure and generating diagnostic commands to determine the root cause.

goal.raw_text: To diagnose a failed device by identifying the specific failure and generating diagnostic commands to determine the root cause.

claims.content: Field Maintenance Staff
The system must be initialized and monitoring devices.
A device failure must have been detected and tracked by the system (indicated by a non-zero 'Command Failure Count').
The Field Maintenance Staff must be logged into the system with appropriate Personnel Security Level permissions to access diagnostic functions.
The system detects a device failure during the monitoring process, resulting in an increment of the Command Failure Count.

trigger.raw_text: The system detects a device failure during the monitoring process, resulting in an increment of the Command Failure Count.

claims.content: The Field Maintenance Staff accesses the system interface to view device status information.
The staff identifies the specific failed device by reviewing the 'Device Status' (Entity #13) and 'Command Failure Count' tracked by the 'Monitor Devices' function.
The staff selects or creates a 'Diagnostic Command' (Entity #14) associated with the failed device.
The system processes the command request through the 'Process GUI Commands' function, validating the staff's 'Personnel Security Level' (Entity #20).
The system transmits the 'Device Sensor Command' to the 'RLCS Field Devices'.
The system receives 'Device Sensor Status' and initialization data from the field device.
The system updates the 'Device Status' and logs the transaction in the 'Device Command Log' (Entity #10).

If the 'Diagnostic Command' fails to execute or returns an error status, the system increments the 'Command Failure Count' and routes the failure data to the 'Track # of Failed Device Commands' function.
If the device is determined to be non-responsive after diagnostic attempts, the Field Maintenance Staff may generate a 'Problem Work Order' (Entity #26) to schedule physical repair or replacement.
If the 'Device Sensor Status' indicates an alarm condition rather than a communication failure, the system triggers the 'Set Alarms' process based on the 'Device Alarm Criteria' (Entity #6).
If the 'Diagnostic Command' execution results in a failure or error status, the system captures the 'Command Failure Data' and routes it to the 'Track # of Failed Device Commands' function (3.2.2.5).
Upon receiving 'Command Failure Data', the system increments the 'Command Failure Count' associated with the specific device.
The system updates the 'Device Status' (Entity #13) to reflect the alarm or failure condition based on the received sensor data.
The system generates an entry in the 'Device Command Log' (Entity #10) recording the failed diagnostic attempt, including the date, time, and operator ID.

If the 'Device Sensor Status' indicates an alarm condition rather than a simple communication failure, the system triggers the 'Set Alarms' process (3.2.2.3) utilizing the defined 'Device Alarm Criteria' (Entity #6).
The 'Device Status' (Entity #13) of the diagnosed device is updated to reflect its current operational state or failure condition.
A record of the diagnostic attempt, including the date, time, and operator ID, is created in the 'Device Command Log' (Entity #10).
If the diagnosis reveals an alarm condition, the system status reflects this based on the 'Device Alarm Criteria' (Entity #6).
If the device is confirmed as non-responsive or requiring physical intervention, a 'Problem Work Order' (Entity #26) may be generated and linked to the relevant personnel.
